_comment: The Content-Security-Policy that next.config.ts is expected to build, directive by
directive, as an exact set of sources per directive.
This file exists because the repo has already shipped a CSP regression, this week:
commit ffa99bc, 'fix(security): the live CSP still allowed two soon-to-be-strangers'
domains'. The guard that was supposed to catch it never opened the file that sets the
policy. So this is an exact-set comparison, not a 'does it contain' one — a directive
that GAINS a source fails just as loudly as one that loses a source.
generated formula strings with new Function(). That is the single reason, it is the
reason sast-dynamic-code-sinks refuses a second eval-class sink, and if that call ever
goes then 'unsafe-eval' should go with it — which is a change to this file, made by a
person, not a drift nobody notices.
This pins the SOURCE. The headers actually served are a separate question with a
separate answer: the static export deploy gets them from Apache/.htaccess, and
scripts/security-smoke.mjs already probes the live ones.
